q1_issues.issue: The verb "appears" is dropped entirely — no appear event is reified, so its lemma is unrecoverable — and the clause is encoded as a static LocatedIn containment, a route the instruction set reserves for "is located/situated in" and the bare postural verbs (lie/sit/stand/hang/lean/perch/rest), which "appear" is not among; a ledger is also a document, not a containing place.

(Most early sk_ledger_1 ledger) claims the unique maximum for a plural set and puts a group witness in the entity slot without the (Member <entity> <class>) companion the superlative rule requires — a group is not a member of its members' kind.

"Watch" is a bare capitalized class word, which Names and casing makes a common noun by default with no Name atom (name-hood needs the capitalized run to exceed the bare class word, or a different word to state the kind).

q2_gaps: textual-occurrence predication ('the phrase appears in / occurs in / is found in <document>') — the stative-locative verb list that routes to LocatedIn does not include it, and nothing says whether such a clause instead reifies an event with an In / Location oblique

attributive superlative over a PLURAL set ('the earliest surviving ledgers') — Most is the unique maximum of one individual and AmongMost is 'one of the ADJ-est'; a set-denoting superlative has no licensed form

a capitalized bare class word used as a PREMODIFIER ('Watch ledgers') — the capitalized-common-noun default (common noun, no Name) and the proper-noun-premodifier rule (Name + Possession) point at different encodings, with the compound-kind route (watch_ledger, genus ledger) a third
notes: The phrase's own typing, the definite-plural group, and the distributed "surviving" modifier rule are all right. The defects are the dropped verb, the plural superlative, and the unlicensed Name atom.
